Under cost_of_capital.missing it prints: "the cost of equity needs a beta and a price: no price series was given: the forward track's price source is Tiingo, and without its token no series is fetched". So there is no enterprise value, equity value or value per share for the bear, base or bull case, and I do not estimate one. The parts of the cost of capital that need no price are on file: a risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}, an equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium|pct}, a pre-tax cost of debt of {cost_of_capital.pre_tax_cost_of_debt|pct} and a tax rate of {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}. What is missing is the beta, the market value of equity, the cost of equity and the capital weights, so an override of the cost of debt would not have helped. The run stopped at the discount rate, not at my drivers: every scenario's terminal growth sits below the risk-free rate. The bridge from enterprise value to equity value would have started from total debt of {ratios.solvency.total_debt} and net debt of {ratios.solvency.net_debt}, a net cash position. Nothing on file says whether the price sat below, inside or above what my drivers would give, and I do not guess.

So this run cannot say what growth the price already assumes. What can be set side by side is the company's record, its guidance and my base driver. Fiscal-year revenue grew at a three-year compound rate of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}, held down by the fiscal 2023 decline of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct}, and at a five-year compound rate of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_five_year_compound|pct}. Fiscal 2025 grew {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.revenue_growth|pct}, the trailing four quarters grew {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, and the latest quarter grew {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} against the year-ago quarter. The quoted guidance puts the coming quarter's year-over-year growth a little above the trailing-four-quarter rate and below the latest quarter's, and it covers one quarter only. most_sensitive.reading: No sensitivity grid and no scenario values were computed, so this is not a measured sensitivity. It is the driver where my base case departs furthest from the filed record. The base year-ten operating margin is above every fiscal year on record, including the fiscal 2021 high of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.4.operating_margin|pct}. It is also far above both the trailing {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} and the three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}. It rests on a larger Data Center share, the run-off of acquired-intangible amortization and research spending spread over a larger revenue base, not on the company's past. Across the cases it runs from just below the fiscal 2021 high in the bear case to well above it in the bull case. In all three cases share-based compensation, {earnings_versus_cash.share_based_compensation_over_revenue|pct} of revenue, stays inside the margin as a cost.

most_sensitive.reading: This is also unmeasured, because neither the grid nor the reverse DCF was computed. Of my six drivers, year-one growth has the widest spread between the bear and bull cases, and through the straight-line fade it sets revenue in every year up to year ten. The bear case sits well below the trailing-four-quarter {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct} but above the three-year compound {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}. The bull case sits above the trailing rate and below the latest quarter's {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct}. In the record only fiscal 2021, at {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.4.revenue_growth|pct}, grew faster. The terminal rate at the other end of the fade matters most when set against the discount rate, and that rate is not on file, so its weight cannot be judged here either.

accounting_adjustments.reading: How much the accounting adjustments moved value was not computed, because no value was computed. The accounting analyst wrote two adjustments, both reducing cash flow and both marked as not recurring. It wrote no earnings adjustment, because the calculator has no field for the unrealized gain on newly listed equity. Python applied both adjustments to quality-adjusted free cash flow and refused neither. The first removes the payables build that MD&A attributes to timing, {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.cash_flow_statement_change}. The second undoes the acquisitions term of {terms.cash_flow_families.acquisitions}, which is negative only because the fiscal 2025 acquisitions line is missing. After both adjustments and after share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation}, quality-adjusted free cash flow is {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}, against simple free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple}. That moves a trailing cash measure, not value per share. In the base and bear cases my year-one reinvestment rate already assumes the payables build reverses.
